value: Study population: 15 semi-isolated Yanomami individuals from Brazil (Yanomami/Brazil), age and gender information collected
Comparative groups: 8 Yanomami from Venezuela, 24 Matses, 12 Tunapuco, 44 urban US individuals
Sample type: single stool sample per subject collected in morning, stored in sterile containers
Sequencing method: HiSeq 2500, total ~219 million reads, ~14 million reads per sample
Bioinformatic tools: Kraken for taxonomy, LEfSe for LDA analysis, SUPER-FOCUS for functional classification
Ethical approval: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation Ethics Research Committee No. 638/11, CONEP No. 16907
Key findings: Yanomami/Brazil showed higher abundance of regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence functions compared to other traditional groups
Lifestyle: semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers practicing hunting, fishing, gathering, swidden horticulture; diet low in fat/salt, high in fruits, fiber, sylvatic animals
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 15 semi-isolated Yanomami individuals from Brazil...Yanomami from Venezuela, n=8...Matses, n=24...Tunapuco, n=12...urban individuals from the United States, n=44...single stool sample...HiSeq 2500 sequencer...Kraken...LEfSe...SUPER-FOCUS...Ethics Research Committee No. 638/11...CONEP No. 16907...higher abundance of gene families involved in regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence...semi-nomadic hunter–gatherers...diet is low in fat and salt, and high in fruits, fiber
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata describing study design, population characteristics, sequencing methodology, and key microbiome findings not captured by specific structured fields.

host_species.evidence_quote: The Yanomami is the largest semi-nomadic hunter–gatherer group of the Americas...Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
host_species.section: Abstract; Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
host_species.notes: Host species is inferred to be human (Homo sapiens) from the description of the Yanomami as a human indigenous group; not explicitly stated in the paper but necessarily implied.
